title: Fur Elise (opening motif, arranged for absolute beginners)
subtitle: 16-bar beginner arrangement: melody with a single bass note per bar
trains: The famous opening motif read at a gentle tempo with eighth notes at most, over a single left-hand bass note per bar - the hands barely need to coordinate.

provenance.author: Musicanyya practice material
provenance.basedOn: Beethoven, Fur Elise, WoO 59 (public domain, composed c. 1810), opening motif only. The pickup and bar 1 pitches were checked against the Mutopia Project's public-domain LilyPond engraving (piece-info id 931, fur_Elise_WoO59.ly, typeset by Stelios Samelis) and against this library's existing intermediate arrangement (public/library/repertoire/intermediate/fur-elise-theme.musicxml).
provenance.note: A different, much simpler arrangement from the intermediate Fur Elise item, not a shortened copy of it: note values are doubled (16ths -> 8ths) and the metre is renotated from 3/8 to 3/4 (both changes needed to bring the shortest value and metre inside the Beginner caps), the left hand is reduced to a single sustained bass note per bar and rests entirely under the fast opening figure (mirroring Beethoven's own texture there), and the famous chromatic E-D#-E-D# hook is stated only once, in the pickup and bar 1, so the piece's accidental rate stays inside the Beginner cap (at most 2 per 16 measures). In bar 1 the middle E5 of the motif is written as a quarter note rather than an eighth (Beethoven's own rhythm there is a straight run of eighths); this is a deliberate rhythmic simplification, not just a pitch quote, so the run of same-value notes stays inside the Beginner cap of 4 (a rest cannot break such a run for this library's level checker, since a rest never becomes a sounding onset - only a longer note does). Bars 2-16 are our own simple, fully diatonic (natural A minor, no accidentals) continuation built from the theme's tonic/dominant outline, and bars 9-16 repeat bars 5-8 to reach the specified 16-bar length - not a transcription of Beethoven's actual bars 9-16, which are harmonically and rhythmically too demanding for this level. 17 written measures (a one-beat pickup plus 16 bars) at quarter = 60.
